newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries open slightly lower, NAPM awaited.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries open slightly lower, NAPM awaited.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries opened unchanged to slightly lower amid cautiousness and profit-taking preceeding a busy calendar of economic data and a day before a scheduled Federal Reserve policy meeting.

The first releases the market will see are those on U.S. personal income and consumption in December. The former is expected to be up 0.8 percent, the latter forecast to be up 0.5 percent. In November, each rose 0.5 percent.
The indicator expected to draw the most attention is the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index.
The January NAPM index, due at 1000 EST/1500 GMT, is forecast at 53.0 versus 53.8 in December. A reading above 50 points to an expanding economy. A reading below 50 indicates some contraction.
The NAPM index and its sub-indices are closely watched because they reflect activity in the nation's manufacturing sector and also because the information for the month just completed is so timely.
In early dealings, the 6-1/2-percent 30-year benchmark Treasury bond was quoted down 2/32 at 96-9/32. Its yield stood at 6.79 percent, unchanged from Friday's close.
At the same time that the market gets the NAPM, it also gets U.S. contruction spending data for December, expected to be down 0.7 percent after a 1.9 percent jump in November.

"Certainly NAPM will be the most important data," said Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A. "Last month it took the market by surprise because, like most of the data in December, it was stronger than expected."
Stiles said of the sub-indices, the market is most concerned about the prices paid component and data on delivery times.
"Greenspan is very interested in those numbers," he said.
Stiles noted that some of the regional NAPM indices showed jumps in the prices index.
But he said I.D.E.A. is looking for a reading of 50.0 on prices paid index, down from 51.5 in December.
Stiles said a lot of shorts were squeezed out of the market on Friday and that the market's direction will depend on the prices and delivery times components of the NAPM.

Many economists, including Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, believe that the delivery times component is an indicator of potential bottlenecks, and therefore possible inflationary pressures, in the economy.
If the prices component of the NAPM index continues to rise above 50, that could pressure the Fed to raise interest rates later in spring, Stiles said.
If the significant NAPM sub-indices ease slightly, the market will try to test 112 on the March bond futures and 6.75 percent on the 30-year bond yield, he said.
"Then dealers could step up and try to lighten up ahead of the refunding," Stiles said.
The Treasury will sell three-, 10- and 30-year securities next week in its quarterly financing operation.
The Federal Open Market Committee, the policy-making arm of the Fed, will meet on Tuesday and Wednesday. Most economists expect it to leave monetary policy unchanged.

At the short end of the maturity range, three-month bill rates were unchanged at 5.02 percent. Six-month bill rates were down two basis points to 5.06 percent. Year-bill rates were unchanged at 5.28 percent. Two- and five-year notes were unchanged at 99-29/32, yielding 5.93 percent, and down 2/32, yielding 6.27 percent, respectively.
Ten-year notes were down 3/32 to 99-29/32, yielding 6.51 percent.
